input: This results passage describes the performance of a shell-and-tube exchanger that heats cooling water in a refinery preheat train, bringing together the main thermal figures that characterise the unit. The duty of the exchanger is 1780 kW. The hot stream enters at 180 °C and leaves at 130 °C, while the cold stream, namely the cooling water, enters at 35 °C and leaves at 60 °C. The log-mean temperature difference for the exchanger is 107 K, and the installed area is 25.2 m2, giving an overall coefficient of 660 W m-2 K-1. Taken together, these figures provide a useful overall picture of the thermal performance achieved by the exchanger under the conditions considered. It is also worth noting the position in relation to fouling. Fouling was assessed from a single 90-day run, and no cleaning cycle has yet been completed. This means that the fouling position is based on a limited operating period and has not been followed through a full cycle in which the exchanger is cleaned and then returned to service. Overall, the reported values describe the exchanger as tested, while the fouling assessment remains limited by the fact that it rests on one run and on an operating history that does not yet include cleaning. The distinction between what has been measured and what remains untested is an important part of the picture. The thermal figures are presented as a coherent set, and they allow the reader to see how the exchanger is performing in terms of duty, temperature change and overall heat-transfer performance. The fouling position, by contrast, is necessarily more provisional, because the evidence comes from a restricted portion of the operating history and does not yet show the condition of the exchanger after a cleaning intervention has taken place.
target: A shell-and-tube exchanger in a refinery preheat train heats cooling water at a duty of 1780 kW. The hot stream enters at 180 °C and leaves at 130 °C; the cooling water enters at 35 °C and leaves at 60 °C. At a log-mean temperature difference of 107 K, the installed area of 25.2 m2 gives an overall coefficient of 660 W m-2 K-1. The coefficient is therefore the value consistent with the stated duty, area and temperature difference for this exchanger. Fouling was assessed from a single 90-day run. No cleaning cycle has been completed. The fouling position is thus the position observed over one run, before any cleaning has intervened. It does not describe the exchanger after cleaning, and it does not show how fouling develops across repeated cycles of operation and cleaning. The reported performance and the fouling assessment also rest on different spans of evidence. The duty, stream temperatures, area and coefficient belong to the stated exchanger condition. The fouling statement belongs to the run that was observed. Keeping those bases separate matters when the figures are used: the thermal values characterise the exchanger at the reported condition, while the fouling conclusion is limited to the single run and to a history with no completed cleaning cycle. The passage also separates the exchanger as a heat-transfer device from the exchanger as a fouling surface. As a heat-transfer device, it is described by the balance between the two streams and by the coefficient that reconciles duty with area and temperature difference. As a fouling surface, it is described only by what one run showed. Those are different kinds of statement. The first can be checked internally, because the reported quantities belong to one consistent thermal picture. The second cannot be extended beyond its run without new evidence, because fouling is a history-dependent condition and the history available here contains no cleaning event. The result is a complete thermal description with a deliberately narrow fouling conclusion attached to it.
